However, the critical criteria for stick\u2010slip instability in mining\u2010affected faults remain unclear. In this paper, by constructing a mechanical model of fault slip induced by mining\u2010disturbed overburden structure instability, and incorporating the rate\u2010and\u2010state friction (RSF) law, we propose a critical mechanical criterion for fault stick\u2010slip instability, revealing the initiation mechanism of such instability. Based on the geological conditions of a specific coal mine, a numerical model was established using FLAC3D to simulate mining in the footwall and hanging wall of a normal fault. The evolution characteristics of key mechanical parameters, such as shear stress and normal stress of the fault rock mass, were analyzed to explore the critical state characteristics of normal fault stick\u2010slip instability under mining disturbances. The results indicate that under the conditions set in this study, the fault stick\u2010slip reaches a critical state when the fault pillar support pressure peaks. The fault slip magnitudes are as follows: footwall mining (2438\u2009mm) >\u2009hanging wall mining (220.1\u2009mm), suggesting that footwall mining is more prone to inducing slip. The numerical values of the critical mechanical criterion for fault stick\u2010slip are in good agreement with the shear\u2010to\u2010normal stress ratio curves obtained from the numerical simulations, thereby validating the reliability of the theoretical model. This study provides ideas for the early warning of fault\u2010slip\u2010induced dynamic disasters in coal mine
